frenchReader: Emma et Tom prennent le petit-déjeuner dans un café à Oaxaca.
Le serveur Luis demande : Vous êtes prêts ?
Emma : Nous ne sommes pas encore prêts.
Emma : Je ne mange pas de viande et Tom ne mange pas de produits laitiers.
Tom : Je ne mange jamais de cacahuètes, je suis allergique.
Luis : Je vais demander à la cuisine s'ils utilisent des noix ou des cacahuètes.
Luis : Les chilaquiles verts sans crème ni fromage ne contiennent ni viande ni produits laitiers.
Luis : Les tortillas de maïs ne contiennent pas de gluten.
Emma : Un autre café avec plus de lait sans lactose et moins de sucre, s'il vous plaît.

sourceNotes: Source is immutable. The 17 English cards and 9 English Reader lines are kept in source order and kind; the forms and modes use the exact source English.
Setting is kept as Oaxaca. The private draft's move to Lyon is a France-specific substitution and is rejected.
The source Reader has no English title, only the Spanish title 'Desayuno sin carne en Oaxaca'. readerTitleFrench translates that Spanish title.
Source card 3 carries a note that 'peanut' is a Mexican word (el cacahuate; el maní elsewhere). French uses cacahuète, with arachide as an alternate for the plant.
Source card 9 ('another') warns against 'un otro' in Spanish. The French equivalent agrees in gender: un autre / une autre.
Source card 17 notes Spanish's double negative (no... nada). The French analogue is ne ... rien, used in frenchCards and the Reader-independent card.

Draft Reader lines 6 to 9 and the passage title were rewritten away from source (invented 'cannot confirm' and 'won't eat anything' lines). They are not used here; frenchReader is rebuilt line by line from the source English.
Forms use the full source English line for both english and readerLine, so each pair is exact; the speaker label is retained.
Source Reader provides Spanish verb paradigms for comer, estar, tener and usar. This candidate has no French verb paradigms, so the French verb progression is incomplete.
internalDomainNotes: The source's allergen and dietary claims (green chilaquiles without cream or cheese having no meat or dairy; corn tortillas not containing gluten; the nut and peanut question) are unverified. The lesson is language practice and is not allergy information for learners.
Learners must not rely on this lesson for food safety. Staff confirmation of ingredients and cross-contact is required in any real setting.
Draft gloss notes on cacahuète, arachide, aux and de-after-negation were not carried into the source-bound cards; they are not source material and need native French review before use.
The lesson is private and unreviewed. No native French review has been completed.
residuals: French verb paradigms for manger, être, avoir and utiliser are not included. The progression is incomplete against the Spanish source paradigms for comer, estar, tener and usar.
Native French review is open. Reviewed status is false.
No audio is verified and no qualified approval exists. Learner gates are all false.

Prêts is written in the masculine plural for the mixed group in 'Vous êtes prêts ?' and 'Nous ne sommes pas encore prêts.' Agreement for an all-female group (prêtes) is not represented in source-bound text.
Dialogue register is vous for the server and the group, which is natural fr-FR but has not been checked by a native reviewer.
